one_month_reasoning: The one big event in the window is Q3 2026 earnings on 2026-10-28, before the open (call at 1pm ET) [4]. Guidance is $9.3-9.4B in sales and $0.70-0.71 post-split adjusted EPS [1,2]. Three things point to a beat and a Q4 guide above consensus: a Q2 book-to-bill of 1.23, IT datacom expected up mid-teens sequentially [3], and strong reads from the rest of the chain over the summer (TE's datacenter orders +70%, Credo +115%, NVDA guiding Q3 to $108B) [5-9]. Amphenol also has a long record of beat-and-raise. Against that, expectations are high and the stock is 4% below its 52-week high, and AI-trade sell-offs have hit on strong prints before (Celestica's Q2) [8]. So I tilt only slightly positive: median about $86.3 (+0.7%) with a lognormal sigma of 12.5% for the month. That is a little below annual vol/3.5 (13%), but the earnings jump keeps it near that level. I keep the distribution close to symmetric because a confident call on earnings direction is expensive if it is wrong.

fair_value.method: Weighted 60/40: forward P/E ($3.84 2028E EPS x 24x = $92) and forward EV/EBITDA (2028E EBITDA $14.8B x 17x, less about $10B net debt, over 2.58B shares = $94). This is the value on 2027-10-01, priced on the next 12 months' earnings.

inputs_detail.derivation: Implied by Oakridge's 25.2x forward P/E at $82.57 (82.57/25.2 = $3.28). Cross-check: the Q3-26 guide of $0.705/qtr [2] annualizes to $2.82, and growing that ~17% gives about $3.3.

In line with consensus 2027 revenue growth of 18.4% [15] plus a little operating leverage, then slower as revenue gets larger. The chain (TE FY27 backlog [5], ~$1T 2027 hyperscaler capex [10,11]) supports another year of growth into 2028, but at a slower pace.
Today's forward P/E is 25.2x [15]. I take off about 1x because growth slows from 50%+ to the high teens. Bernstein's $99 target [20] and GF Value of $80.73 [19] roughly bracket where this lands.

inputs_detail.derivation: Adjusted operating margin of 29.8% in Q2-26 [1], plus about 3.5% D&A, minus some caution because CommScope mix and higher capex [3] dilute it. 42.1 x 0.305 = $12.8B for 2027E. Growing ~15% gives $14.8B for 2028E.
Today's EV/EBITDA is 23.0x [15]. I compress it to 17x on forward EBITDA as growth normalizes, which is consistent with the 24x P/E above.
Q2-26: $18.8B debt less $4.7B cash = $14.1B [1]. I assume about $4B of paydown from FCF ($1.2B/qtr [1]) after dividends and buybacks.
1.289B pre-split [1] x 2 after the Sept-2026 2-for-1 split [2]

bear.story: AI capex digestion begins in 2027. Investors who already sold Alphabet on capex ROI in July 2026 force cuts. Amphenol's IT datacom book-to-bill falls below 1, and Rubin midplane or CPO adoption takes copper content from Amphenol instead of adding to it. EPS stalls around $3.1 and the multiple drops to about 19x.

base.story: Hyperscaler capex grows toward about $0.9-1.0T in 2027. Amphenol keeps or gains content on Rubin (Evercore estimates +20-40%), and CommScope keeps scaling. 2028E EPS is about $3.85 and the multiple compresses moderately to about 24x.

bull.story: NVDA's forecast of +70% FY28 growth comes true and 1.6T/200G-per-lane ramps keep orders far above billings. Amphenol stays at 50%+ growth into early 2027, NTM EPS reaches about $4.4, and the multiple holds near 29x.

thesis_break_reason: $58 is below the 52-week low ($59) and about 18x 2027E EPS. A price there would most likely mean the market sees AI interconnect orders rolling over (book-to-bill below 1, or hyperscaler capex cuts) or a structural loss of copper content to optics, not ordinary volatility.

reasoning: Company facts: Q2-26 sales were $8.8B (+55%, +30% organic), with orders of $10.7B (book-to-bill 1.23). IT datacom was 43% of sales, up 89%. Q3 is guided to $9.3-9.4B and $0.70-0.71 post-split EPS [1,2,3]. Industry reads are uniformly strong. TE's datacenter networking orders rose 70% against 30% revenue growth, which points to an FY27 backlog [5,6]. Credo is up 115% and guides FY27 growth above 85% [7]. Celestica expects 2027 growth to accelerate beyond 65% [8]. NVDA's data center revenue rose 117% and it guided Q3 to $108B [9]. Bishop data show connector billings +21% YTD with bookings ahead, a 1.07 book-to-bill and a $34B backlog, and North American bookings up 54% [12]. 2026 hyperscaler capex is about $720B, with 2027 estimates near $1T [10,11]. The Manifold 2027-capex market was thin and resolved N/A, so I treat it only as a sentiment lead [14]. Risk from Rubin's cable-free midplane is two-sided: X and the press suggest Amphenol supplies the midplane connectors [16,17,18]. So the chain supports 2027 growth, but much is already priced in: about 25x forward and 23x EV/EBITDA [15], with some valuation skeptics (Oakridge $54 intrinsic [15], GF Value $81 [19]). Fair value is $93 (P/E and EV/EBITDA, both with moderate multiple compression). I modeled the 12-month distribution as a mixture: 78% lognormal with median $95 and sigma 0.30 (the base and bull cases), and 22% lognormal with median $62 and sigma 0.35 (an AI-digestion bear case). That gives an overall median of about $89 and an effective vol near the stock's 46% realized vol, with a fat left tail. Research was limited: Twelve Data estimate and target endpoints were paywalled, and two CNBC pages returned 403.
